# name: # One row per layer. Layers of one name are summed (amix, no auto-normalise), then
# Variant v of a layer takes the v-th file matching file_glob (sorted, wraps around) and the v-th
# value of start_ms (optional, comma list, wraps; where to seek in that file before trimming silence).
# fade_in_ms (optional) softens a layer that enters mid-sound; a seek alone gets 2 ms.
# Globs are matched case-insensitively against "<pack>/<path inside the pack>" (pack = bundle folder or zip).
# Fitted 2026-10-03 on the Mac against the real Sonniss GDC 2024 (parts 1-2) and Kenney Interface packs.
# Hit times come from tools/audio/library_catalog.tsv plus a 5 ms peak scan: start_ms sits ~10 ms
# before each transient peak, so the impact lands at t=0 (the hit sound fires on contact; the swing
# is the separate whoosh played at the start of active frames). Picked by envelope, brightness and
# name — not by ear yet: the listening pass is Santos's (bash tools/audio/audition.sh).
# light: cardboard thump (classic foley punch) + anime "noise punch" + wet slap + a touch of sub
# heavy: two-handed axe into flesh (4 takes) + anime punch + stone crack + cinematic sub
# block: metal shield taking a hit (4 takes) + dull cardboard body
# whoosh: cotton rips have the rise-and-fall of a swish (each start sits before the rise, never on the
# peak — a hard onset reads as a tear); a slice of a heavy sci-fi whoosh adds the low end
